# identical. > *The two cars are identical except for their license plates.*. > *This is the identical room we stayed in last year.*. 1. Also called: **numerically identical**. > *Cicero and Tully are identical*. 2. Also called: **quantitatively identical**. "Collins English Dictionary — Complete & Unabridged" 2012 Digital Edition © William Collins Sons & Co. Ltd. ### Origin of identical. First recorded in 1610–20; from Medieval Latin *identic(us)* identic + -al 1. How does *identical* compare to similar and commonly confused words? > Fake air bags can look identical to genuine components. Two spies agree to use a certain book. They both have identical copies. > The act allows for an identical bill that passes the Commons twice to become law, even without the Lords' consent.
